transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Umbria CTO), Aisha Khan (ML Infra), Liam O'Reilly (Prod)

Auto-summary: quick intro; high-level fit; deep dive on compat (vLLM/TGI) and security; agree next steps for benchmarks and security deep-dive.

[00:00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood Inference team. With me is Priya, our systems SE.
[00:00:10] Carlos Mendez: Thanks, Jordan. Carlos here, CTO at Umbria. We wanted use this call to see, uh, what the options are between staying with our current provider and moving to something more predictable cost/latency wise.
[00:00:22] Priya Rao: Awesome. Quick agenda — we'll do intros, ask about your current stack and pain points, then we can map to Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and finish with pilot proposals and open questions. Sound good?
[00:00:34] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Quick note: we're running a mix right now — primary chat endpoints on OpenAI and a small fleet of internal vLLM nodes for lower-latency local inference during peak windows.
[00:00:45] Liam O'Reilly: And product wants consistent latencies under 150 ms p95 for interactive features — cost can't spike more than 30% relative to current spend.
[00:00:55] Jordan Kim: Got it. Two clear levers: latency SLO and unit economics. Quick qual: vertical — you're B2B analytics for finance, right? Data residency maybe a thing?
[00:01:06] Carlos Mendez: Yes enterprise finance — some EU customers require data residency, and we have an internal compliance requirement for customer data not to be stored beyond 30 days.
[00:01:15] Priya Rao: Ok, good to note. For residency and retention, Private or Dedicated with VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS typically fits. Hosted can also comply depending on region and contractual add-ons.
[00:01:27] Jordan Kim: Can you walk us through the vLLM/TGI usage? How much of the traffic is routed there vs OpenAI?
[00:01:34] Aisha Khan: Roughly 40% of interactive queries go to vLLM on prem, mostly short prompts, the rest to OpenAI for long dialogue and embeddings. We're experimenting with TGI in a sandbox but haven't put it in prod.
[00:01:46] Priya Rao: That split actually makes sense. Our compatibility playbook supports model portability from vLLM/TGI and hosted OpenAI-style APIs. There are some nuance with KV cache handling and attention kernel differences that affect latency and memory profiles.
[00:01:58] Carlos Mendez: Can you expand on that? We ran into cache thrashing when we tried to lift vLLM models into a cloud runtime.
[00:02:04] Priya Rao: Sure. Two things — continuous batching and KV cache eviction policies differ between runtimes. If you port a vLLM-backed model to our hosted runtime, Redwood's runtime preserves per-request KV semantics but the default batcher aggregates differently. We provide configuration knobs — per-route batching windows, prefix cache reuse, and also fallback model variants if memory constraints hit. Sometimes the transcription notes — kv cache vs kia cache — but point being: we tune batching/kv to match your latency/cost envelope.
[00:02:35] Liam O'Reilly: So would we need to change model checkpoints or fine-tune again?
[00:02:39] Priya Rao: Mostly no. For the usual decoder-only and chat models from common families, identical checkpoints work. Exceptions: custom quantization artifacts or operator differences in TGI vs vLLM might need a very small compatibility pass — typically recompile/quantize for the target runtime. We include a compatibility checklist in the eval.
[00:02:56] Carlos Mendez: Okay. Security is big for us — SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration for customer keys. How do you handle that across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
[00:03:08] Jordan Kim: Short answer: all three support SSO and RBAC. Hosted has enterprise add-ons for SAML and per-customer KMS via CMKs; Dedicated offers isolated GPU pools and VPC peering; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane with HSM/KMS integration on-prem or in your VPC. We can share SOC 2 + ISO docs.
[00:03:26] Aisha Khan: Do you expose raw token logs? Our compliance team forbids storing full prompts longer than 30 days, and we need redaction at source.
[00:03:33] Priya Rao: You can configure retention at the token level, and we have built-in redaction/hooks to strip PII before logging. For Private, you can also keep logs within your network and only export aggregated cost/latency metrics.
[00:03:44] Liam O'Reilly: Pricing — curious about the Dedicated trial you mentioned. Can you run a pilot with our 3-node vLLM workload?
[00:03:51] Jordan Kim: Yes — typical pilot: we mirror a subset of traffic for parity tests, or we can stage a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity for two weeks. We'll provide a cost estimate based on your throughput and model memory footprints.
[00:04:06] Carlos Mendez: On parity — we need to reproduce answers at least 95% of the time compared to our current models. How do you measure eval parity?
[00:04:13] Priya Rao: We use a combination of automated evals: exact-match / semantic similarity thresholds, and human-in-the-loop sampling for critical prompts. We'll import your ground-truth prompt set and run A/B comparisons with statistical significance thresholds. We'll share the parity template spreadsheet (Priya: pointer to sheet).
[00:04:30] Priya Rao: (small pause) I'll upload the parity template and a sample benchmarking sheet after the call — it's a shared Drive link, we usually ask for a representative 200-300 prompt set covering short/long/edge cases.
[00:04:42] Aisha Khan: We'll prepare that. Also curious about function calling and tooling — we depend on structured JSON responses for downstream parsers. Any known differences in function-calling semantics?
[00:04:53] Priya Rao: Function calling semantics are supported. Hosted mirrors OpenAI-style function spec; Dedicated/Private can be configured to enforce strict JSON schemas and post-processing hooks. There are occasional tokenization differences that can cause trailing commas or whitespace — small cleanup steps in our eval pipeline fix those.
[00:05:08] Liam O'Reilly: Real-world question: last month we did a dry run moving off a managed provider and saw latency regressions under tail load. How would Redwood prevent that?
[00:05:17] Priya Rao: A few mechanisms — smart routing (route to lower-latency model variants), autoscaling tuned for burst windows, and prefix/KV reuse to cut cold-starts. For tight p95 SLOs, Dedicated with pre-warmed capacity typically gives the most predictable tails.
[00:05:33] Carlos Mendez: What's the integration effort? We have infra as code and a CI/CD pipeline that deploys models and monitors.
[00:05:40] Jordan Kim: Integration is usually 2–6 weeks for a pilot: API keys, route definitions, model pinning, and then one sprint to run parity tests. We have SDKs and IaC modules for Terraform/CloudFormation to make it scriptable.
[00:05:53] Aisha Khan: Are there any gotchas with TGI specifically? We've seen operator mismatches when moving between TGI versions.
[00:06:00] Priya Rao: With TGI, the important bits are custom ops and attention kernels. If you're on a bleeding-edge TGI build, we'll likely recommend compiling the model with our recommended operator set or use a vetted runtime image we provide. We can help with the compatibility pass.
[00:06:14] Liam O'Reilly: How do you handle fallbacks? If a heavy request can't be served on the preferred model, do you degrade gracefully?
[00:06:20] Priya Rao: Yes — policy-based fallbacks: degrade to a compressed/quantized variant or route to a lower-cost region. For strict correctness we can also return a 429 and trigger a queued async job. It's configurable per-route.
[00:06:33] Carlos Mendez: Ok. Team, any concerns on cost — how transparent is the per-token and per-embedding breakdown? We need line-item clarity for chargebacks.
[00:06:41] Jordan Kim: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route, per-model breakdowns. You can export CSVs for chargeback. For Dedicated we also offer flat monthly capacity pricing plus overage.
[00:06:54] Aisha Khan: Curious about model catalog — do you host open models? What about licensed models from Anthropic?
[00:07:01] Priya Rao: We maintain a catalog of open weights and vetted third-party images. For licensed Anthropic models, we support integration when customers bring appropriate licenses — we can run them under Dedicated or Private depending on license terms.
[00:07:14] Liam O'Reilly: Great. On the pilot — would Redwood help run a side-by-side where some traffic is mirrored and some routed live?
[00:07:20] Jordan Kim: Yes, we typically do a mirror + evaluate approach: mirror production traffic to the pilot environment for N days, run A/B sampling for outputs, and track latency/cost. We'll include a baseline dashboard for parity metrics.
[00:07:33] (crosstalk) Carlos Mendez: That exactly what we want — minimal risk but measurable metrics.
[00:07:37] Priya Rao: One operational note: for mirror traffic, you need to scrub or anonymize PII before sending to external systems unless you're running Private.
[00:07:46] Aisha Khan: Noted. We'll scrub. Also procurement — what kind of contract lead times?
[00:07:51] Jordan Kim: For Hosted small accounts it's straightforward; for Dedicated and Private, typical procurement cycle is 4–8 weeks depending on SOC/Legal review. We'll surface standard legal templates and a security bundle to accelerate review.
[00:08:04] Liam O'Reilly: Ok, let's capture next steps.
[00:08:08] Jordan Kim: Recap: Jordan will send hosting comparison deck and estimated pricing; Priya will share benchmark spreadsheet and parity template; Umbria will provide sample prompt set and latency/cost matrix; schedule security deep-dive next week. We'll also scope a 2-week Dedicated trial pending procurement.
[00:08:25] Carlos Mendez: That aligns. Any final technical docs we should expect?
[00:08:29] Priya Rao: I'll attach: compatibility checklist (vLLM/TGI notes), parity template, sample IaC modules, and our SOC2/ISO summary.
[00:08:37] Jordan Kim: Ok thank you all — we'll follow up with the links and proposed calendar invites.
[00:08:42] Aisha Khan: Thanks. Bye.
[00:08:44] Carlos Mendez: Bye.

Notes/Artifacts referenced:
- Umbria parity template (Drive) — will be shared by Priya
- Hosting comparison deck (Redwood) — Jordan to send
- Benchmark spreadsheet and IaC repo link — Priya to share

End of recording.
